title: Big-O Time & Space Complexity
interviewAnswer: Big-O describes how runtime or memory grows with input size. I use it to compare algorithms asymptotically, while remembering constants, cache behavior and real input sizes still matter in practice.
keyPoints: Know O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²).
Distinguish worst, average and amortized complexity.
why: Big-O Time & Space Complexity appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Know O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²).
deepDive: Big-O describes how runtime or memory grows with input size. I use it to compare algorithms asymptotically, while remembering constants, cache behavior and real input sizes still matter in practice. Distinguish worst, average and amortized complexity. Analyze both time and memory. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Sorting ten million rows with an O(n log n) algorithm is usually viable; an accidental nested O(n²) comparison can become catastrophic.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Big-O Time & Space Complexity make?
How would you validate or debug Big-O Time & Space Complexity in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
